description: We’re two Ukrainian sisters working across borders—one in Vilnius, an optical engineer pursuing a master’s in Photonics and Nanotechnology, and the other in Ukraine, an aspiring aerospace engineer studying for her bachelor’s degree. Together, we connect an interest in how satellites observe our planet with a drive to make that information useful on the ground. Our goal is to harmonize satellite data and turn it into timely predictions that help first responders protect communities.
summary: FireWatch is an analyst dashboard that harmonizes fragmented satellite records (NASA FIRMS) into a unified fire activity calendar. It enables real-time map tracking, historical pattern analysis, and early warnings for responders, scientists, and land managers to monitor wildfires and agricultural burns effectively.
details:
FireWatch is an interactive web application and analyst dashboard that integrates and harmonizes multi-year satellite wildfire observation data into a unified fire activity calendar.

  • Functionality: The system integrates real-time active fire and hotspot satellite data (specifically via NASA FIRMS VIIRS) along with weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Users can select an area of interest on an interactive map (powered by Leaflet.js and Esri basemap tiles), view geospatial patterns, analyze historical burn data, and receive prompt early warnings through a minimalist control panel.
  • Solves the critical problem of inconsistency and fragmentation in historical satellite records across different sensors, transforming complex statistical data into an intuitive, visual fire activity calendar.
  • Provides early warnings for emergency and fire services, scientists, and land managers. Helps proactively anticipate critical periods, minimize the risks of large-scale forest and agricultural fires, and protect ecosystems.
  • Languages & Logic: Python, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3.
  • Cartography & Frontend: Leaflet.js, Esri topographic basemap tiles, interactive popups, and geolocation.
  • Data & Backend: NASA FIRMS WMS layer, Open-Meteo API, SQLite database for processing and storing geospatial information.
  • We created not just a regular map with points, but a full-fledged "fire activity calendar" and analytical dashboard that combines historical analysis with live satellite streams in a single interface.
  • During development, we focused on performance, UI usability for emergency services (fast loading, intuitive risk indicators), and the accuracy of harmonizing data from different satellites for reliable forecasting.
